results.text: Proteus mirabilis >100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible: ceftriaxone, cephalexin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Resistant: nitrofurantoin.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text:
Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without IV or oral contrast, renal stone protocol.

Findings: A 7 mm calculus is present in the proximal right ureter, about 3 cm below the ureteropelvic junction. Mild right hydronephrosis and hydroureter proximal to it, with perinephric fat stranding. No calculus remains in the right kidney. Left kidney normal in size without calculus or hydronephrosis. Bladder decompressed, otherwise unremarkable. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and gallbladder unremarkable on this noncontrast exam. Appendix normal. No free fluid or free air. Uterus and adnexa unremarkable. Visualized lung bases clear. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 7 mm obstructing proximal right ureteral calculus with mild right hydronephrosis and perinephric stranding.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 01/12/2026 05:50. Disposition: observation under urology.

CC: right flank pain.

HPI: 35F woke around 4 am with abrupt, severe right flank pain running down into the groin. Nauseated, has not vomited. Noticed red urine on the way in. She was evaluated by urology in July for recurrent infections and has a known right kidney stone.

PMH: recurrent UTIs, right renal stone. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother with stones, father with HTN. SH: teacher; never smoker; rare alcohol.

Triage: T 37.8 C (100.0 F), BP 130/85, HR 98, RR 18, SpO2 99% RA.
Exam: uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no guarding, no rebound.

UA: alkaline, pH 8.0, cloudy, LE and nitrite positive, WBC >100/hpf, large blood, RBC 75/hpf.
CBC, BMP: within normal limits. Urine hCG negative.
CT A/P without contrast (stone protocol): 7 mm proximal right ureteral stone, mild right hydronephrosis, perinephric stranding; no remaining right renal stone.

ED course: ketorolac 15 mg IV and ondansetron 4 mg IV with good relief. Low-grade temp with infected-appearing urine above an obstructing stone, so ceftriaxone 1 g IV after culture. Discussed with on-call urology, who will decompress tonight.

Impression: obstructing right proximal ureteral stone with urinary tract infection.
Disposition: urology.

documents.title: Urology Observation Discharge
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Admitted to observation 01/12/2026, discharged 01/13/2026.

Procedure 01/12/2026, evening: cystoscopy and right ureteral stent placement (6 Fr x 24 cm). Cloudy urine drained from the right side on stent passage. No complications.

Course: afebrile overnight, pain controlled, tolerating diet. Ceftriaxone continued until discharge. Urine culture pending at discharge, final 01/14: Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to cephalexin.

Discharge meds: cephalexin 500 mg four times a day for 10 days; oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 one every 6 hours as needed, #8; ondansetron 4 mg ODT as needed.

Plan: definitive ureteroscopy in about 3 weeks once the infection is treated. PCP follow-up next week. Return for fever over 101, inability to keep fluids down, or uncontrolled pain. The stent may cause urgency and some blood in the urine; this is expected.

documents.title: Post-ED check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED and urology records came in yesterday. Called pt: home since Tuesday, out of work this week. No fever. Pain mostly controlled, using about one pain pill a day, mostly at night. Stent makes her feel like she has to pee all the time, some pink urine, which they told her to expect. Taking cephalexin, no missed doses. Office follow-up booked 1/20.

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 1/12 in the ER with an obstructing 7 mm R proximal ureteral stone (the renal stone urology saw in July has moved), infected urine, Proteus again. Stented that night, home 1/13. Records reviewed.

Now: back at school today. No fevers since discharge. Flank pain gone. Stent irritation - urgency, frequency, mild discomfort at the end of voiding, occasional pink tinge. Down to Tylenol only, has 5 oxycodone tablets left and will hold onto them until after the procedure. Cephalexin day 8 of 10.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Mild R CVA tenderness, much less than described in ED. Abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Right ureteral stone, stented, with Proteus UTI - responding. Finish cephalexin. BMP today to make sure kidney function recovered. Ureteroscopy scheduled 2/3.
2. Infections and stone are almost certainly linked; hopefully clearing the stone clears the infections. Will want stone analysis.
3. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Right Ureteroscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Ambulatory surgery center, outside urology group
Date of procedure: 02/03/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: right proximal ureteral calculus, stented.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: cystoscopy, right stent removal, right rigid and flexible ureteroscopy, holmium laser lithotripsy, basket extraction of fragments, right ureteral stent placement on extraction string.
Anesthesia: general. Antibiotic: cefazolin 2 g IV. Preop urine culture 1/29: no growth.

Findings: stone in the proximal right ureter, unchanged in position, fragmented with the laser. Fragments extracted with a basket and sent for analysis. Inspection of the right collecting system showed no residual fragments. Mild ureteral edema at the stone bed. No ureteral injury.
EBL minimal. No complications.

Plan: stent on string, patient will remove at home on 2/10 (instructions given). Tamsulosin not prescribed. Stone analysis pending. Follow-up in clinic in 6 weeks with renal ultrasound and urine culture.

documents.title: Calculus analysis report
documents.author: outside laboratory
documents.body:
Reference laboratory, infrared spectroscopy calculus analysis. Specimen: right ureteral stone fragments, collected 02/03/2026.
Composition: magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) 80%; carbonate apatite 20%.
Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Stone results?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the stent out last week on my own, which was weird but fine. I saw a stone result posted. What does struvite mean?

documents.title: RE: Stone results?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good work on the stent. Struvite is the type of stone that forms from infection: the Proteus bacteria make the urine alkaline and the stone builds up from that, and then the stone keeps seeding infections. So the fact that it is now out is the real fix. Urology will check an ultrasound and a urine culture in March to make sure nothing is left. If you get infection symptoms in between, send a urine sample before starting antibiotics.

reports.text: Right kidney 10.8 cm, left kidney 11.0 cm. Normal cortical thickness and echogenicity bilaterally. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing echogenic focus to suggest a stone in either kidney. Bladder partially distended, normal wall, no intraluminal stone; ureteral jets seen bilaterally.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Urology follow-up letter, visit 03/16/2026

Kelly returns six weeks after right ureteroscopy and laser lithotripsy for a 7 mm proximal ureteral stone, which analyzed as 80% struvite and 20% carbonate apatite. She removed her stent herself as planned. No flank pain, fevers or urinary infection symptoms since. No medications.

Vitals normal. Abdomen benign, no CVA tenderness.
Renal ultrasound today: no stones, no hydronephrosis on either side.
Urine culture: no growth.

Assessment: stone-free after treatment of an infection stone.
Plan: continue high fluid intake. Obtain a culture with any urinary symptoms and treat per sensitivity. Renal ultrasound in 6 months, sooner with symptoms. Return here after that study.

Urology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 35, teacher, first week of summer break.

Interval: right ureteral stone in January (ER, stent, then ureteroscopy 2/3). Stone was struvite. Urology follow-up in March: ultrasound clear, culture negative. She has not had a single urinary infection since January, the longest stretch in two years. Drinking a big water bottle twice a day. No flank pain, dysuria or hematuria.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: unchanged (mother stones, father HTN).
SH: never smoker, alcohol a drink or so a month.
Gyn: regular cycles. Pap due (last 2023).

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP normal, weight steady. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. Extremities without edema. Skin normal. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.
Urine dip in office: LE, nitrite and blood negative.

A/P:
1. Kidney stone - treated, stone-free on March US. Moved to resolved on the problem list. Urology plans repeat ultrasound around September.
2. Recurrent UTI - none in 5+ months since the stone came out. Keep on list for now. Culture before antibiotics with any future episode.
3. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids today. Pap today. Vaccines up to date; flu and COVID in the fall.
4. Follow-up visit in the fall.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kelly, your blood work from the physical was all normal, and the Pap came back negative. Next Pap would be in three years. Enjoy the rest of the summer.
